subject: Request: custom SLA addendum — traffic shaping & regional failover carveout
messages:
From: Elaine Brooks <elaine.brooks@medflowhealth.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ben.howard@medflowhealth.com
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom SLA addendum — traffic shaping & regional failover carveout

Hi Kimberly,

Following our onboarding call last week, MedFlow would like to request a tailored SLA addendum to our enterprise MSA/SOW addressing two items that are material to our regulatory and availability posture: traffic shaping during scheduled peak windows and a regional failover carveout for our primary US-East workloads.

High level asks from procurement/ops:
- A short exhibit that describes a traffic-shaping policy for scheduled batch ingestion (daily 02:00–05:00 UTC) and peak burst handling, with clear latency SLOs during the window.
- A regional failover carveout that allows our app to route to a secondary region with a documented recovery time objective and a credit schedule if failover is required.
- Language we can include in the Order Form / Exhibit that is compatible with our procurement flow and DocuSign.

Attached is our current MSA/SOW redlines (MedFlow_MSA_SOW_Redlines.pdf) and a one-page diagram of our expected traffic patterns. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide an exhibit and a proposed clause for the Order Form? Also: what evidence (telemetry/audit) would you expect to include to operationalize the carveout?

We are targeting legal review by next Wednesday (6/5) so a draft from your side by end of day Monday (5/30) would be ideal.

Thanks,
Elaine Brooks
Head of Procurement — MedFlow Health
elaine.brooks@medflowhealth.com
+1 415-555-0198

Attachments: MedFlow_MSA_SOW_Redlines.pdf, traffic_shaping_diagram.png

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear summary and the redlines. Very actionable.

Quick plan:
1) Internal scoping and proposed exhibit language from us by EOD Monday (5/30).
2) We’ll include an Order Form snippet you can paste into DocuSign and a short evidence list (telemetry and report cadence).
3) If acceptable, we can route the exhibit via DocuSign with a single signature flow for the Order Form addendum.

A couple quick clarifying Qs for your engineering/legal teams:
- For the traffic-shaping window, do you require hard latency SLOs (e.g., 95th pct latency <= 250ms) during the window, or a best-effort performance band with credits only for queueing/backpressure?
- For the regional carveout, is MedFlow proposing automatic failover (DNS-level) or manual failover with runbook steps? That affects how we define the RTO and evidence.

Looping in David (runtime/ops) and Marissa (contracts) to draft the language and the credit schedule. We’ll mark any operational constraints up front.

—Kimberly

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Request: custom SLA addendum — traffic shaping & regional failover carveout

Kim / Marissa — draft notes below (technical constraints + suggested wording). Saving to redwood_sla_snippet_v1.txt and will attach to the outbound.

Technical summary:
- Traffic shaping (scheduled window 02:00–05:00 UTC): we can support a windowed SLO for requests that are tagged with a customer-provided header (x-mf-batch: true) to enable priority queuing. For untagged traffic we will continue standard routing.
- During the window, continuous batching and prefix caching reduce per-token cost but increase tail latency variability; we can guarantee 95th percentile token-response latency <= 350ms for interactive calls and <= 1.2s for large batched jobs (defined as > 10k tokens).
- Regional failover: we support automated failover policies but need an agreed runbook. For automated failover, expected RTO = 30 minutes (detect + warm KV cache) with caveats for model load and cold-start quantized variants.

Suggested Order Form / Exhibit excerpt (plain text):
Traffic Shaping Exhibit (MedFlow) — Scheduled Window
1. Definitions: 'Scheduled Window' means 02:00–05:00 UTC daily. 'Tagged Job' means requests that include the agreed customer header.
2. During the Scheduled Window, Redwood will apply traffic-shaping to prioritize Tagged Jobs and will maintain the following SLOs: 95th percentile interactive request latency <= 350ms; 95th percentile large-batch request latency <= 1.2s when a Tagged Job flag is present.
3. Credits: Failure to meet the above SLOs in a calendar month will entitle MedFlow to a service credit equal to 5% of that month's Services fees for each SLO missed, up to 25% monthly cap.

Regional Failover Carveout (excerpt):
1. Redwood will provide a documented failover playbook and will support a regional failover option with an RTO of thirty (30) minutes for automated failover scenarios attributable to Redwood infrastructure failure.
2. Evidence: Redwood will provide post-incident telemetry, routing logs, and a recovery timeline report within 7 business days.

Operational notes:
- Credits are measured from Redwood’s telemetry. We will include sampling of token latency and request traces for the relevant time window.
- If MedFlow requires a stricter RTO (e.g., < 30 minutes), we need to agree on additional reserved capacity (Dedicated pool) and a corresponding pricing uplift.

—David
David Kim
Director, Inference Ops — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Request: custom SLA addendum — traffic shaping & regional failover carveout

Hi Elaine — attached is a concise draft exhibit and an Order Form snippet you can paste into DocuSign. Summary of what we included:

- Traffic Shaping Exhibit: scheduled window definition, tagging mechanism, SLOs (95th pct interactive <= 350ms / large-batch <= 1.2s), and a credit schedule (5% per miss, 25% cap).
- Regional Failover Carveout: automated failover RTO = 30 minutes, required runbook steps, and evidence deliverables (telemetry + post-incident report within 7 business days).
- Operational caveat: if MedFlow wants sub-30-minute RTO or guaranteed cold-start warm caches, that requires Dedicated capacity and a pricing uplift.

Attachments included: medflow_msasow_draft_v2.pdf (we pasted the exhibit into the SOW), redwood_sla_snippet_v1.txt (raw excerpt), traffic_shaping_diagram.png.

DocuSign route: we can prepare a single signature Order Form flow. If you confirm the attached language, we’ll upload to DocuSign and send via the link below.

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/redirect/abc123-medflow-sla
Drive (internal reference): https://drive.redwoodinference.com/teams/procurement/medflow/sla-drafts

Two small asks before we send to your legal:
1) Can your engineers confirm the tagging approach (x-mf-batch header) and whether any existing proxies will strip custom headers?
2) Confirm who at MedFlow will sign the Order Form (procurement or legal contact).

If you’re good with the draft I’ll start the DocuSign flow Monday morning to hit your legal review target.

—Kimberly

Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
